_comment: Thresholds for the Lighthouse job in CI (§10.1). Every number here was
measured against the real site before it was written down — a gate set
by guesswork is either meaningless or flaky, and a flaky gate is worse
than none because people learn to ignore it.
accessibility and seo are ERRORS at 1.0 because both are rule-based and
deterministic: the same page scores the same on any machine, so a drop
is a real regression somebody introduced. Both pages measured 100 once
the two defects this job found were fixed.
performance is a WARNING and deliberately not a gate. It is timing on a
shared CI runner and moves several points between identical runs.
Failing a merge on that teaches people to re-run until it passes.
The real performance regression on a site like this is somebody
committing a four-megabyte hero photograph, and bytes ARE deterministic.
So maxBytes is the performance gate. The measured weights are 178 KB
(home), 159 KB (packages) and 330 KB (guide); 900 KB leaves room for
ordinary growth and still catches an unoptimised image on sight.
_lighthouseVersion: Pinned exactly, and fetched with npx rather than added to
package.json. Scoring changes between Lighthouse releases, so a
floating version turns this gate red for no code reason — which is the
one thing it must not do. Kept out of the dependency tree because it is
CI-only and never shipped: as a devDependency its 170-odd transitive
packages would join `npm audit` in the security job, where an advisory
in a tool that only ever visits our own site would block an unrelated
merge. Bump it here, deliberately, and re-measure the thresholds below.
_metricsComment: The three §10.1 targets, which the plan named and nothing reported.
cumulative-layout-shift is an ERROR, unlike the performance score.
It measures layout, not timing: a page that jumps under the reader's
finger jumps the same way on any machine, and it is the regression a
carelessly sized image actually causes. 0.1 is the plan's own target
The other two are timing and so are warnings, for the same reason the
performance score is. INP has no lab equivalent at all — it needs a
real finger on a real screen — so total-blocking-time stands in for
it, which is what Lighthouse itself recommends and is not the same
thing. Measured: LCP 2.3 s, CLS 0, TBT 10 ms.
